claim_formal: ∃K ∀k≥K ∀r≥2: W_r(k) > k^{c·k·⌊log₂ r⌋}, c=10⁻⁵ (hence W_r(k)^{1/k}→∞ for each fixed r)

quote_A.text: There is an absolute integer $K_0$ such that, for every integer $k\ge K_0$ and every integer $r\ge2$, \[ W_r(k)>k^{c k\lfloor\log_2r\rfloor}

quote_B.text: giving a quantitative positive resolution of Erdős's superexponential-growth question, including the two-color case

notes: c=10^-5 explicit, threshold K0 not explicit (hence ∀^∞ by rule 2; 'effective' refers to c only). Erdős question cited from a 1980 paper (p.90,(2)), not a numbered database entry, so P2 rather than P3. Companion bound for large r (Theorem transfer:large-r) is a side result. Cites Campos–Fox–Schildkraut, which credits ChatGPT, but the headline does not build on it.

claim_formal: ∃ finite simple graph G with ≥1 edge: t(H,G) < p(G)^66, for the explicit 35-vertex 66-edge bipartite incidence graph H

quote_A.text: There is a finite simple undirected graph \(G\) with at least one edge such that \[ t(H,G)<p(G)^{66}. \]

quote_B.text: We disprove Sidorenko's conjecture with a bipartite graph on 35 vertices and 66 edges

notes: H is explicit; G is shown to exist by sampling a kernel (not given explicitly). Also refutes the Skokan–Thoma forcing conjecture and gives amplification corollaries.

claim_formal: ∃q₀ ∀ prime q≥q₀ ∃ intersecting (q+1)-partite (q+1)-uniform hypergraph H with all parts of size q+1 and τ(H)=q+1 (> (r−1)ν(H)=q)

quote_A.text: There exists $q_0$ such that, for every prime $q\ge q_0$, there is a finite intersecting $(q+1)$-partite $(q+1)$-uniform hypergraph $H$

quote_B.text: This disproves Ryser's covering conjecture, even for intersecting hypergraphs with equally sized parts.

notes: Two manuscripts: balanced prime-order version (headline) and an s^n+1 version (s≡2 mod 3). Corollary refutes Gyárfás's monochromatic tree-cover conjecture. Lean BalancedRyser matches headline; RyserCovering/RyserOddExtensions match the second paper.

claim_formal: ∀r,m ≥1 ∀ coloring χ:ℕ→[r] ∃ a₁<…<a_m: FS({a_i}) ∪ FP({a_i}) monochromatic

quote_A.text: for every finite coloring of the positive integers and every positive integer k, there is a k-element set whose nonempty subset sums and nonempty subset products all have the same color

quote_B.text: We prove Hindman's finite sums and products conjecture

notes: Ramsey-type existence (∀ coloring ∃ monochromatic configuration) coded M2. Corollary gives distinct expressions.

quote_A.text: For every integer \(n\ge3\), \[ \crn(K_n)=Z(n)

quote_B.text: We prove the Harary–Hill conjecture

notes: Family bundles Harary–Hill (K_n) and Zarankiewicz/Turán brickyard (K_{m,n}); both settled O1 and both Lean-formalized. Hebbar–Mangam 2018 earlier claimed both formulas, but the paper treats those claims as lacking a lower-bound argument, so not O9.

claim_formal: ∀d≥3 ∃c_d>0 ∀ finite P⊂ℝ^d with n≥2 points: |Δ(P)| ≥ c_d n^{2/d}

quote_A.text: there is a constant \(c_d>0\) such that every finite set \(P\subset\mathbb R^d\) of \(n\ge2\) distinct points satisfies \[ |\Delta(P)|\ge c_d n^{2/d}. \]

quote_B.text: This resolves the higher-dimensional Erdős distinct-distances conjecture positively.

notes: Order n^{2/d} is attained by the integer grid (classical), so M9 'sharp up to constants' is a defensible alternative to M8; the constant c_d is not determined.

claim_formal: ∀ε>0: sup_{P⊂ℝ², |P|=n} #{x∈P : |D_x(P)| < n^{1−ε}}/n → 0 as n→∞ (all but o(n) pins see ≥ n^{1−ε} distances)

quote_A.text: For every fixed $s>0$, one has $F_n(s)\longrightarrow0$ as $n\longrightarrow\infty$.

quote_B.text: We prove the weak pinned Erdős distinct-distance conjecture.

notes: Lean states the main theorem F_n(s)→0, which implies the headline corollary (pins) by a short argument, so it is coded 'same'. Second manuscript: planar unit distances u(n)=O(n^{4/3−δ}) (P4/O7-type record improvement, also Lean-formalized). The theorem gives no rate of decay. Erdős 1957 'Problem 16' is in a paper, not a database.

claim_formal: ∀ Coxeter systems (W,S),(W',S') ∀ u≤b, u'≤b' ∀ poset isomorphism ι:[u,b]→[u',b']: P_{u,b}(q) = P_{u',b'}(q)

quote_A.text: is an isomorphism of abstract Bruhat interval posets, then their equal-parameter Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials satisfy \[ P^W_{u,b}(q)=P^{W'}_{u',b'}(q). \]

quote_B.text: This resolves the full combinatorial invariance conjecture positively.

notes: Matrix is an implication 'iso ⇒ equal polynomials' (M1). M7 (identity of named objects) is a possible alternative. Corollary covers all subintervals and R-polynomials.

claim_formal: ∀ natural unit interval graph G: χ_G(X;q) = Σ_{σ∈D_G^0} q^{ginv(σ)} e_{θ_G(σ)}, so every e-coefficient ∈ ℕ[q]

quote_A.text: We prove that the chromatic quasisymmetric function of every natural unit interval graph is elementary-positive over $`\mathbb N[q]`$.

quote_B.text: This resolves the elementary-positivity part of the Shareshian–Wachs conjecture.

notes: Lean asks for an explicit witness θ (∀G ∃θ, prefix ∀∃); the headline is positivity (∀, M1). The e-positivity part is a standalone conjecture (q-analogue of Stanley–Stembridge), coded O1; the unimodality part of Shareshian–Wachs is not addressed, so O5 is a possible reading. Corollary: Hessenberg cohomology as a permutation module.

quote_A.text: For every fixed integer $s\ge6$ there is a constant $C_s>0$ such that, for every $\varepsilon>0$ and every sufficiently large integer $t$

quote_B.text: The theorem resolves the sharp logarithmic-exponent question for \(r(5,t)\).

notes: Two manuscripts: s=5 and s≥6, both in Lean. The log exponent is determined exactly (M9). The case s=4 is still open (Mattheus–Verstraëte gives (log t)^4 against the upper bound's (log t)^2), so the family settles s≥5 of a question posed for all fixed s: O5 restricted_range by rule 6. If the question is taken per s, rule 7 gives O1. The constant factor is not determined.

quote_A.text: There is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that \[ R(Q_n)\le C2^n \qquad\text{for every integer }n\ge0. \]

quote_B.text: This resolves positively the hypercube Ramsey conjecture of Burr and Erdős.

notes: The linear order is matched by the classical 3·2^{n−1}−1 lower bound, so M9 'order determined' is an alternative. C is not given numerically.

claim_formal: ∀ finite A⊂ℝ^d (s≥2 points, affine span ℝ^d): A is Ramsey ⇔ ∃P∈Mat_{d+1}(F⊗_ℚF) satisfying the tensor evaluation and spatial conditions

quote_A.text: Then $A$ is Ramsey if and only if there is a matrix $P\in\operatorname{Mat}_{d+1}(B)$ such that

quote_B.text: In particular, some Ramsey cyclic quadrilaterals are not subtransitive, disproving the necessity direction of the Leader–Russell–Walters conjectured characterization.

notes: The posed problem is to characterize Ramsey sets. LRW predicted 'subtransitive'; the family refutes that and replaces it with a correct criterion, hence O3. P2 'open classification question' is an alternative reading. Corollaries: subtransitive sets and ≤5 circle points are Ramsey; generic 9 circle points are not. Pálvölgyi's earlier spherical-conjecture counterexample is credited to ChatGPT; the headline does not clearly build on it, so the builds_on_model_output flag is not set.

claim_formal: ∀ nonempty finite oriented graph D ∃v∈V(D): |N₁⁺(v)| ≤ |N₂⁺(v)|

quote_A.text: Every nonempty finite oriented graph has a vertex \(v\) such that \[ \abs{N_1^+(v)}\leq \abs{N_2^+(v)}. \]

quote_B.text: This resolves Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture positively.

notes: ∃ vertex with a property: M2, with M1 a possible alternative. Weighted forms and directed-triangle consequences are given as corollaries.

claim_formal: ∃C>0 ∀k≥1 ∀ finite loopless k-edge-connected multigraph G (|V|≥2) ∃ spanning tree T ∀ cut S: |δ_T(S)| ≤ (C/k)|δ_G(S)|

quote_A.text: There is a universal constant \(C>0\) such that, for every integer \(k\ge1\), every finite \(k\)-edge-connected undirected multigraph without loops and with at least two vertices has a spanning tree \(T\)

quote_B.text: This resolves the strong thin tree conjecture.

notes: The headline is the existence of a thin tree (M2); a bound reading (M8) is possible. The companion manuscript gives a deterministic polynomial-time construction (M10, also in Lean as AlgorithmicThinTrees) and thin-and-cheap rounding of fractional cuts.

claim_formal: ∀ finite X ∀ nonempty proper increasing family F⊆2^X: q_f(F) ≤ 25·512⁴·q(F)

quote_A.text: \[ q_f(\F)\le25\cdot512^4\,q(\F). \] Both thresholds use the budget $1/2$.

quote_B.text: We prove Talagrand's conjecture that integral and fractional expectation thresholds are within a universal constant factor, with the same covering budget.

notes: The family bundles three results: integral vs fractional thresholds (headline, Talagrand Conj. 6.3), Talagrand's discrete-convexity conjecture (k=2^75, Lean), and the AHPT graph-decomposition conjecture (which uses the discrete-convexity paper). All three are O1. A comparison within a constant factor is coded M8; M1 is an alternative.

claim_formal: ∀n≥2 ∀ graph H with h≥1 edges and ≤n vertices: p_c(n,H) ≤ min{1, 2048e⁵⁰·p_E(n,H)·(1+log₂h)}

quote_B.text: We prove the second Kahn–Kalai conjecture.

claim_formal: ∀d≥3 ∃D<∞, ε>0, ∃ finite connected pure d-dim complexes X_m with |X_m(0)|→∞, vertex top-degree ≤D, and ‖δ_i f‖ ≥ ε·dist(f,B^i) ∀i<d ∀f

quote_A.text: For every integer d ≥ 3, we construct arbitrarily large finite d-dimensional simplicial complexes with uniformly bounded vertex degrees and uniform 𝔽2 coboundary expansion in every degree below d.

quote_B.text: Together with the known graph and two-dimensional cases, this establishes the existence of bounded-degree 𝔽2 coboundary expanders in every positive dimension.

notes: Posed as Gromov's question and Problem 1.3 of CL2025, which is not a numbered problem list, so P2. The full all-dimensions statement uses the known d=1,2 cases.

claim_formal: ∀d≥3 ∃ deterministic algorithm, ∃n₀(d),k_d ∀ even n≥n₀: it outputs in O_d(n^{k_d}) bit operations a simple d-regular graph G on n vertices with all nontrivial eigenvalues in (−2√(d−1), 2√(d−1))

quote_A.text: the algorithm outputs the adjacency list of a simple $d$-regular graph $G$ on $n$ vertices in $O_d(n^{k_d})$ bit operations

quote_B.text: we give a deterministic algorithm that constructs a simple nonbipartite d-regular Ramanujan graph on every sufficiently large even number n of vertices

notes: The headline is algorithm existence (M10) together with existence of the graphs (M2). The posed problem, deterministic explicit nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs in every degree at all large orders, has no named conjecture in the input, so P2. The O1 reading is uncertain. restricted_range covers even n only (needed for odd d). Corollary: every large size up to +1.

claim_formal: ∀n≥1: (∃ real circulant Hadamard matrix of order n) ⇔ n∈{1,4}

quote_A.text: a real circulant Hadamard matrix of order \(n\) exists if and only if \(n\in\{1,4\}\).

quote_B.text: We prove the circulant Hadamard conjecture: a real circulant Hadamard matrix has order 1 or 4.

notes: The substance is non-existence for n>4 (M4). The 'iff' form makes M6 (complete list of orders) a reasonable alternative. The Barker-sequence conjecture follows by combining with Turyn–Storer/Schmidt–Willms for odd lengths. Lean EvenBarker covers that corollary.

claim_formal: ∀ finite simple cubic bipartite planar 3-vertex-connected graph G ∃ Hamiltonian cycle in G

quote_A.text: Every finite simple undirected graph that is cubic, bipartite, planar, and \(3\)-vertex-connected has a Hamiltonian cycle.

quote_B.text: We prove Barnette's conjecture

notes: Coded M2 (existence of a Hamiltonian cycle); M1 'G is Hamiltonian' is an alternative. Corollaries: edge avoidance, and 3-edge paths in Pfaffian cubic bipartite graphs.

claim_formal: ∃C>0 ∀n ∀ simple graph G on n vertices: E(G) partitions into ≤ Cn cycles and single edges

quote_A.text: There is an absolute constant \(C>0\) such that, for every finite simple undirected graph \(G\) with \(n\) vertices, \(E(G)\) has a partition into at most \(Cn\) parts

quote_B.text: This resolves the Erdős–Gallai cycle decomposition conjecture positively.

notes: A linear upper bound on the decomposition number (M8). M2 'existence of a small decomposition' is an alternative. The linear order is optimal (trees). Corollary: Eulerian graphs decompose into ≤ Cn cycles.

claim_formal: ∀k≥2 ∃c_k>0 ∀ intersective h∈ℤ[x] of degree k with positive leading coefficient ∃C_h,N_h ∀N≥N_h ∀A⊆[N]: (A−A)∩h(ℕ₊)⊆{0} ⇒ |A| ≤ C_h N^{1−c_k}

quote_A.text: whenever $N\ge N_h$ and $A\subseteq[N]$ satisfy \[ (A-A)\cap h(\N_+)\subseteq\{0\}, \] one has \[ |A|\le C_h N^{1-c_k}. \]

quote_B.text: This answers the fixed-power question posed by Green and Sawhney.

notes: Three manuscripts: square differences (answers Green–Sawhney's fixed-power question, Lean SquareDifference), general intersective h (headline), and prime arguments. Lean covers only the square case, hence weaker. The headline generalizes the square answer, so O8 is an alternative to O1. Not P4/O7, since it answers the posed question of a fixed power saving rather than improving a record exponent.

claim_formal: ∃ε>0,C,n₀ ∀ even n≥n₀ ∀ n-point P⊂ℝ² with no three collinear: h(P) ≤ C n^{4/3−ε}

quote_A.text: There exist absolute constants $\varepsilon>0$, $C<\infty$, and $n_0$ such that, for every even $n\ge n_0$ and every $n$-point set $P\subset\mathbb R^2$ with no three collinear, \[ h(P)\le C n^{4/3-\varepsilon}. \]

quote_B.text: This gives a power saving over the classical $`O(n^{4/3})`$ bound for planar halving lines.

notes: The proof is explicitly nonquantitative (ineffective ε, C, n₀). Corollary: k-set bound O(n(k+1)^{1/3−ε₀}). The lower bound is n·exp(Ω(√log n)), so the problem remains open.

claim_formal: ∀ finite graph F ∃C_F,Δ_F ∀ F-free graph G with Δ(G)≥Δ_F: χ_DP(G) ≤ ⌈C_F Δ/log Δ⌉

quote_A.text: For every fixed integer r ≥ 4, we prove that every Kr-free graph of sufficiently large maximum degree Δ has correspondence chromatic number $`O_r(\Delta/\log\Delta)`$.

quote_B.text: This resolves the Alon–Krivelevich–Sudakov coloring conjecture in the stronger correspondence-coloring form.

notes: Second manuscript: the AEKS independence conjecture α ≥ c_r n log d/d for K_r-free graphs (Erdős Problem 802, P3/O1). Only that result is in Lean (CliqueFreeLog), hence 'different' relative to the coloring headline. The headline is proved in a stronger (DP) form than conjectured, still coded O1.

claim_formal: ∃ countably infinite E ∃ self-dual infinite matroids M₀,M₁ on E: ∀ independent I₀,I₁: I₀∪I₁≠E, and (M₀,M₁) has no packing/covering partition (in ZFC)

quote_A.text: In ZFC, there exist a countably infinite set $E$ and two infinite matroids $M_0,M_1$ on $E$

quote_B.text: This disproves the unrestricted infinite matroid packing/covering and intersection conjectures and answers Joó's question for two partitional matroids negatively.

notes: Also refutes the unrestricted infinite Matroid Intersection Conjecture and answers Joó's Question 1.5 negatively. As a by-product, it constructs a self-dual uniform infinite matroid in ZFC (open questions of Bowler–Geschke and Gollin–Joó). Nash-Williams' finitary conjecture is untouched.

claim_formal: ∀n≥2 ∀ nontrivial increasing vertex-invariant graph property P ∀ε∈(0,½): p_{1−ε}(P)−p_ε(P) ≤ 2¹⁹ log(1/(2ε))/(log n)²; analogously O_r((log n)^{−r/(r−1)}) for r-uniform hypergraphs

quote_A.text: p_{1-\varepsilon}(\mathcal P)-p_\varepsilon(\mathcal P) \le \frac{2^{19}}{(\log n)^2}\log\frac1{2\varepsilon}.

quote_B.text: We prove the Friedgut–Kalai sharp-threshold conjecture.

notes: The headline covers graphs and r-uniform hypergraphs. Lean formalizes only the graph threshold-width theorem, hence weaker. The (log n)^2 order is optimal by the FK clique example, so M9 is an alternative. The variance/influence bounds also hold for nonmonotone properties.

claim_formal: ∃ Maker policy σ ∀ legal Breaker play β: Maker owns a copy of Snaky (up to translation/rotation/reflection) within 21 Maker moves on empty ℤ²

quote_A.text: there is one globally legal Maker policy that completes an allowed copy of $S$ within at most $21$ actual Maker claims against every legal continuation of Breaker

quote_B.text: Sieben subsequently gave a finite proof sequence for that handicap and described the ordinary planar problem as undecided at the time

notes: The existence of a winning strategy is the substance; the 21-move count is an upper bound, not claimed optimal. finite_checkable because the strategy is confined to a fixed 251-cell board. Lean SnakyTwentyOne matches (SnakyConditional is the 35-move version). The posed question was 'is Snaky a winner?' (Harary), which the input calls undecided rather than conjectured, so P2.

claim_formal: Random triangle removal from K_n: E[(F_n/n^{3/2} − 1/(2√2))²] → 0 (hence F_n/n^{3/2} → 1/(2√2) in probability)

quote_A.text: \[ \E\left[\left(\frac{F_n}{n^{3/2}}- \frac1{2\sqrt2}\right)^2\right]\longrightarrow0. \]

quote_B.text: This proves the triangle case of the sharp-constant conjecture of Joos and Kühn.

notes: The Joos–Kühn Conjecture 16.2 covers general strictly balanced hypergraph removal; only the triangle case is settled, so O5 restricted_range (rule 6). If the triangle case is viewed as the classical Bollobás–Erdős problem posed on its own, O1 would apply. Uses the Joos–Kühn early-prefix estimates as input.

quote_A.text: For all integers $m\ge n\ge3$ with $(m,n)\ne(3,3)$, \[ R(C_m,K_n)=(m-1)(n-1)+1. \]

quote_B.text: This establishes the cycle–clique conjecture of Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp.

notes: Computer-assisted: the reduction leaves 3,099 finite instances checked by programs. Keevash–Long–Skokan had already left only finitely many pairs open, but the paper's reduction does not rely on their constant.

claim_formal: ∃ explicit 66×66 binary H ∀h≥1 ∃ n_h×n_h binary A_h: dist_H(A_h) ≥ ε_h and N_H(A_h)/n_h^{132} ≤ ε_h 2^{−h}; hence no polynomial removal bound for H

notes: Conjecture 4.5 of Gishboliner–Shapira; it also answers Alon–Ben-Eliezer Problem 1.4 negatively. Corollary: lower bound for canonical testers.

claim_formal: ∃η,c₁>0 ∃n₀ ∀n≥n₀ ∃ n-point P⊂[0,1]²: every triangle of P has area ≥ c₁ n^{−2+η} (refuting Δ(n) ≤ C_ε n^{−2+ε} ∀ε)

quote_A.text: There are absolute constants $\eta,c_1>0$ and an integer $n_0\ge3$ such that \[ \Delta(n)\ge c_1n^{-2+\eta} \qquad\text{for every integer }n\ge n_0. \]

quote_B.text: Thus the almost n−2 upper-bound formulation of Heilbronn's triangle problem is false.

notes: Matrix: a power lower bound (M8) whose constructed point sets refute the 'almost n^{-2}' conjecture, so coded M3 (counterexample precedence); M8 is the close alternative. The exponent is explicit but tiny (Lean: 1/(10^5·K)), hence effective. Lean gives the lower bound only along a sequence n_j→∞, plus the refutation, so weaker than 'every n≥n₀'. P1 with O2: the almost-n^{-2} formulation is refuted, but Heilbronn's problem (the true order) remains open.
